headline.phase: Boundary redrawn: discover leads, compile local MCPs
headline.summary: Agent 1 no longer normalizes services; it finds them and hands over Service Leads with their authoritative sources. Agent 2 compiles each lead into a municipality-specific MCP capability plan. The new boundary is documented on a branch but not yet in code: the crawler still emits service records, main still ships a normalized seed inventory, and Patrick's minigmeind MCP runs outside the repo with one fixed tool surface on dummy data.

system.claim: The common standard is the protocol boundary, not the municipal data model.

stages.name: Discovery
stages.question: What services exist here, and where is the authoritative material?
stages.title: Crawl the municipality, identify services, collect source links — then stop
flow: HTTP fetch, browser only if needed

modules.name: Reconnaissance & crawl strategy
modules.summary: Full, section, directory or discovery crawl chosen per site; strategy and stop reason must be visible.
modules.next: Record chosen strategy and stop reason in the crawl output.

modules.name: HTTP crawler
modules.summary: Bounded same-origin crawl with private-address rejection, redirect validation and URL deduplication. 3 tests on main, 11 in PR #7.
modules.next: Merge PR #7; run on Binn end to end.

modules.name: Browser fallback
modules.summary: HTTP → headless browser → agentic browser, only as each proves insufficient. Manual capture helpers exist; the crawler has no browser path.
modules.next: Add only when an HTTP fetch demonstrably fails on a Batch A site.

modules.name: Service vs. noise
modules.summary: Heuristic classifier: Strahlerpatente is a service, Webcam Binn is not. Tourism/news negatives tested in PR #7.
modules.next: Measure precision on Bosco/Gurin.

modules.name: Source-role classification
modules.summary: Label each source: service_page, form, application_pdf, calendar_pdf, official_portal, external_handoff, contact_page …
modules.next: Add a role field to PageIR output.

modules.name: Source bundle grouping
modules.summary: Agent 1's main semantic task: Abfall + Abfallkalender.pdf + Sammelstellen + Gebühren → one lead. Uncertain grouping stays explicit.
modules.next: Group by link graph + shared labels on Binn first.

modules.name: Service Lead output
modules.summary: The prototype still emits partial service records; it should emit the small Service Lead envelope instead.
modules.next: Simplify pipeline/prototype to write service-leads.jsonl.

modules.name: Structured catalogue adapter
modules.summary: Dübendorf's i-web /dienstleistungen/ catalogue: one adapter could cover many municipalities on the same CMS.
modules.next: Inspect Dübendorf's catalogue structure.

modules.name: Seed inventory (8 municipalities)
modules.summary: Normalized mmp-service-inventory/v0 with capability tags, merged in PR #8. Under the new boundary its 22 official sources are best reused as seed Service Leads.
modules.next: Relabel as seed leads, or retire once Batch A runs.

stages.name: Service Compiler
stages.question: What does this service actually require here, and how should an MCP expose it?
stages.title: Inspect the local sources, understand the local implementation, design the MCP surface

modules.name: Source reader (HTML, PDF)
modules.summary: PageIR parses HTML today. PDF reading is not implemented, and Binn's waste calendar is a PDF.
modules.next: Text-PDF extraction for Ausserberg and Binn bundles.

modules.name: Capability planner
modules.summary: Large model reads one lead + its bundle and decides tools, inputs, source strategy, handoffs and limitations — per municipality.
modules.next: One Ausserberg lead → one plan, by hand-run prompt.

modules.name: Model access
modules.summary: OpenAI gpt-6-luna calls work from main (scripts/test_openai.py). The crawler has a separate Apertus-compatible adapter with fallback.
modules.next: Use one client for the planner; keep the adapter for classification.

modules.name: Small Apertus path
modules.summary: Small model / deterministic layer for classification, page roles, type hints and obvious grouping; big model only for compiling plans.
modules.next: Run the classifier through the adapter against the event endpoint.

modules.name: Capability ↔ tool mapping
modules.summary: Maps ~30 semantic capabilities to minigmeind's fixed tool names. Written for the normalized-inventory model; needs rethinking if tools become per-village.
modules.next: Agree with Patrick how a capability plan lands in minigmeind.

modules.name: Cross-municipality normalization
modules.summary: eCH-0070 and a national ontology are now optional — useful later for indexing and analytics, not needed for the first MCP. ADR-0001 still says canonical.
modules.next: Record the deferral against ADR-0001.

stages.name: MCP Builder
stages.question: Does the plan validate, and can it run safely as tools?
stages.title: Validate the plan, bind allowed sources, generate or configure tools, package the runtime

modules.name: minigmeind MCP (Patrick)
modules.summary: Live MCP with ~31 tools on dummy data — one fixed surface for every municipality. Not committed here.
modules.next: Commit it, or link its repo, so the observatory can see it.

modules.name: Plan validator
modules.summary: The builder, not the model, owns schema validation of mcp-capability-plan/v1.
modules.next: JSON Schema for the plan.

modules.name: Source binding & safety
modules.summary: Each tool may read only the sources its plan names; budgets and security enforced by the runtime.
modules.next: Define how a tool references a source_ref at runtime.

modules.name: Tool generation from plan
modules.summary: Template or configure tools from a validated plan (document_lookup, pdf_table, handoff …).
modules.next: One source_strategy (document_lookup) end to end.

modules.name: Tool contract tests
modules.summary: Every generated tool answers from its sources or says it can't; no fabricated results.
modules.next: Write alongside the first generated tool.

modules.name: Package & hosting
modules.summary: Downloadable package and a stateless public HTTPS endpoint, no citizen query logs.
modules.next: Decide whether minigmeind's hosting is the target.

stages.name: Citizen Experience
stages.question: Can a citizen get an official answer or the right handoff?
stages.title: Apertus / Open WebUI calls the village MCP and routes to official channels

modules.name: Ausserberg scenarios
modules.summary: Five German reference questions, including one that must honestly answer 'not available'.
modules.next: Use as the end-to-end acceptance test.

modules.name: Host connection
modules.summary: minigmeind's tool list shows up in a host (16:43 screenshot). No multi-tool scenario recorded.
modules.next: Record one Ausserberg scenario per host.

modules.name: Apertus as host model
modules.summary: Open question OQ-2: does the public model call MCP tools reliably?
modules.next: Try minigmeind from Apertus.

modules.name: Reference client (Open WebUI)
modules.summary: ADR-0006 forks Open WebUI with an MCP Apps host; the MVP plan runs it unmodified.
modules.next: Decide fork vs. unmodified.

modules.name: Official-channel handoff
modules.summary: Actions route or prepare; they never claim a municipal transaction completed.
modules.next: Include the official URL in every answer.

modules.name: Demo narrative
modules.summary: Same capability, two villages, two different MCP surfaces — the story the new boundary makes possible.
modules.next: Draft once Binn and Zürich-style plans exist.

artifacts.name: Service Leads
artifacts.summary: Which services exist and which authoritative sources to read for each. Small on purpose.

artifacts.name: Capability plan
artifacts.summary: The typed IR of the semantic compiler: which tools this village should get for this service, fed by which sources.

artifacts.name: Village MCP
artifacts.summary: An MCP tailored to one municipality. Binn might get get_collection_calendar; Zürich might get get_collection_date(address). Today only minigmeind exists: one fixed surface, dummy data.

wrap.name: Trust · provenance · Judge
wrap.title: Wraps the whole chain — why do we believe this, and from which source?

modules.name: Source provenance
modules.summary: Publisher, canonical URL, retrieval time, content hash per source; schema and snapshots exist.
modules.next: Write source records from the crawler, not by hand.

modules.name: Service-lead provenance
modules.summary: Where was the service found, was the grouping inferred, which pages were inaccessible. Replaces field-level provenance at this stage.
modules.next: Emit discovery evidence with every lead.

modules.name: Field provenance validator
modules.summary: finalize.py enforces provenance on every populated field of a normalized record. Now a downstream concern for Agent 2, not Agent 1.
modules.next: Reuse its checks for capability-plan sources.

modules.name: Evidence quote check
modules.summary: Quotes are not_checked until a browser pass confirms them.
modules.next: Apply to lead discovery evidence.

modules.name: Judge
modules.summary: Checks capability plans and answers against their sources; build floor decides what ships.
modules.next: Judge one capability plan against its bundle.

modules.name: Injection safety
modules.summary: Page text is data, never instructions — matters more now that a model reads whole source bundles.
modules.next: Fixture page with embedded instructions.

modules.name: Discovery evals
modules.summary: Lead recall and precision against hand-labelled service lists; bundle completeness.
modules.next: Hand-label Binn's services.

operate.name: Operate
operate.title: Keep it alive — rebuild, refresh, deploy, govern

modules.name: Build lifecycle
modules.summary: A build produces data, not code — now: leads + plans; only the builder produces runtime.
modules.next: Give each discovery run a build id.

modules.name: Refresh & last-good
modules.summary: Rediscover on schedule; a failed rebuild keeps the last good MCP.
modules.next: After the first village MCP exists.

modules.name: Deployment
modules.summary: minigmeind is hosted somewhere; nothing from this repo is deployed.
modules.next: Document where minigmeind runs.

modules.name: Governance & sign-off
modules.summary: Does a municipality sign off before publish, and who is publisher of record (OQ-1)?
modules.next: Answer OQ-1.

modules.name: Adoption / GTM
modules.summary: Pitch line: we compile local MCPs instead of building one national dataset.
modules.next: One-page adoption story.

tensions.title: Handoff on main still ships normalized data
tensions.detail: pipeline/handoff (PR #8, 7fc855d) publishes mmp-service-inventory/v0 and calls ingestion 'the evidence and canonical-data layer'. The docs branch says Agent 1 hands over Service Leads and Agent 2 does the understanding.

tensions.title: Fixed tool surface vs. per-village tools
tensions.detail: minigmeind exposes one ~31-tool surface for every municipality, and the capability matrix maps data onto it. The new compiler lets Binn and Zürich get different tools for the same service. Both can coexist only if someone decides where the plan lands.

tensions.title: Commercial baseline vs. Apertus
tensions.detail: Main now calls gpt-6-luna; the pipeline targets a small-Apertus / large-planner split. Fine as baseline → replacement, but it should be written down.

tensions.title: eCH-0070 canonical vs. deferred
tensions.detail: ADR-0001 (accepted) makes eCH-0070 canonical; the new architecture makes cross-municipality normalization optional.

tensions.title: Reference client: fork vs. unmodified
tensions.detail: ADR-0006 forks Open WebUI with an MCP Apps host; the MVP plan runs it unmodified with no MCP Apps cards.

tensions.title: Stale duplicated docs
tensions.detail: pipeline/scrapping/docs/ holds older copies of ARCHITECTURE, BUILD_PLAN, CRAWL_STRATEGIES, SERVICE_MODEL and others; after the service-lead rewrite they contradict the top-level docs.
